_why: stream_table_join.rs:1187-1190's TableMissingDataStrategy::EmitWithNulls arm FABRICATES three column names (id/name/value) with the comment 'for now, just add a few common fields'. It is the last surviving instance of the invented-column class #2000 removed from field_names_for_source. A fabricated name is worse than absence: it can COLLIDE with a real column on the stream side and make a genuinely-invalid reference resolve to NULL instead of erroring. The async sibling graceful_degradation.rs::add_null_fields has ALWAYS taken expected_table_fields; this sync copy simply never threaded it, so the fix is mechanical. Reachability is ESTABLISHED, not assumed: emitting an empty FieldMap from this arm turns test_batch_processing_with_graceful_degradation red with u.id absent, so the batch path reaches this handler and this handler produces the u.* columns.

anchors._note: add expected_table_fields: &[String]; three call sites at :1022, :1153, :1160, all inside functions that already hold a table handle (optimized_table: &OptimizedTableImpl at :961, table: &Arc<dyn UnifiedTable> at :1116)
the ASYNC sibling that already takes expected_table_fields — mirror it, do not invent a second shape
the authoritative column set. NOTE the default impl derives from RECORDS, so an empty table reports NO columns — that is exactly why the test fixture must declare its own (see tests)

blast_radius._note: 4 refs in ONE file: the definition plus three call sites. Genuinely small — the work is the test fixture and the discriminating assertion, not the threading.

grammar_reference._note: No SQL is written or edited.

tests._note: test_batch_processing_with_graceful_degradation is the ONLY test that reaches this handler, and today it CANNOT detect the defect: it asserts u.id and u.name, which are both plausible real columns AND members of the fabricated [id,name,value] set, so it passes either way. Restoring the fabrication would leave the suite green. It must gain a DISCRIMINATING pair — a column declared-but-never-fabricated (must be NULL) and one fabricated-but-not-declared, i.e. `value` (must be ABSENT) — and be verified to FAIL against master.

acceptance: handle_missing_table_data_sync takes the expected field set and NULL-fills from it; the hardcoded id/name/value literals are gone from src/
all three call sites pass the table's own column_names()
MockEmptyTable overrides column_names() — a table with no ROWS still has a SCHEMA, and the missing override is why the fabrication was never caught
test_batch_processing_with_graceful_degradation asserts a declared-but-not-fabricated column is NULL and that `u.value` is ABSENT, and was verified to FAIL against master
the sync and async paths now agree on where the column set comes from
forbidden: do not delete the EmitWithNulls arm or change what strategy is selected — the defect is the invented NAMES, not the strategy
do not weaken test_batch_processing_with_graceful_degradation's existing u.id/u.name assertions; ADD to them
do not invent a second shape for the field set — mirror graceful_degradation.rs::add_null_fields

do not run a revert-check before COMMITTING the production change: `git checkout HEAD -- <path>` on an uncommitted edit destroys it, and on a fresh branch HEAD is master. This destroyed the fix twice during the scoping spike.
do not create a branch: the worktree is already on the branch velo-dispatch cut for you
stop_conditions: you cannot make test_batch_processing_with_graceful_degradation FAIL against master with the discriminating assertions — report it rather than shipping a test that cannot detect the defect
threading the parameter requires changing a PUBLIC signature outside stream_table_join.rs — report it, that is wider than this spec pins
